card.name: Sentence-opening prepositions in news text
card.fires_on: Short prepositions such as In, On, in, on at the start of a news sentence or clause, or just after an organization name. The next word is often a possessive or a time or topic phrase.

modes.label: Sentence-starting In/On
modes.description: A capitalized In or On opens a new sentence in a news story, before a study, topic or day.
modes.example: <<On>> the question of autism, numerous studies conducted

modes.label: Preposition after a name or date
modes.description: A lowercase preposition or comma follows an organization, place or date, leading into a description.
modes.example: The research is based at the Birck Nanotechnology Center<< in>> Purdue's Discovery Park .

card.writes: It pushes toward possessive words like Its and 其 that would follow the preposition or name.
card.plain: It marks little linking words like In or On in news sentences, where a possessive such as its often comes next.
